skills.name: buildQueryString
skills.card:
buildQueryString — Assemble a ?key=value query string from named parameters.
  needs: params: object
  optional: baseUrl: string, sort: boolean
  e.g. "build a query string from these parameters" → {"params":{"name":"Ana","age":34}}

params.label: parameters
params.prompt: Which parameters should I build the query from?

baseUrl.label: base url
baseUrl.description: a URL to hang the query off

sort.label: sort alphabetically
sort.description: put the parameters in alphabetical order

examples: build a query string from these parameters
make a query string with a space in the value
build a query with a repeated parameter
add a search query to this url
build a query string in alphabetical order

skills.name: columnMath

operation.label: operation
operation.prompt: Sum, average, min, max or count?

examples: add up the amount column
what is the average q1
highest value in the score column
sum a column with a blank cell in it
how many rows have a value in name

skills.name: diffJson

left.label: original json
left.prompt: Which JSON should I compare from?

right.label: new json
right.prompt: Which JSON should I compare to?

examples: diff these two json documents
compare two identical json objects
what was removed between these two versions
diff a nested config change
compare two lists of tags

skills.name: filterRows

column.label: column
column.prompt: Which column should I filter on?

value.label: compare to
value.prompt: What should I compare it to?

examples: keep only rows where amount is over 100
show me just the North region rows
filter to names containing "an"
drop everything at or below zero
filter where nothing matches

skills.name: flattenJson
skills.card:
flattenJson — Squash nested JSON down to one level, every key a dot path.
  needs: json: string
  optional: separator: string, arrayIndices: boolean
  e.g. "flatten this json" → {"json":"{\"a\":{\"b\":1,\"c\":2}}"}

arrayIndices.label: expand arrays
arrayIndices.description: expand array items into indexed paths

examples: flatten this json
flatten a nested config
flatten json with an array
flatten deeply nested json
flatten already flat json

skills.name: formatJson
skills.card:
formatJson — Tidy JSON into readable indented form, or squash it onto one line.
  needs: text: string
  optional: style: string, indent: integer, sortKeys: boolean
  e.g. "pretty print this json" → {"text":"{\"a\":1,\"b\":2}"}
examples: pretty print this json
minify this json
format with 4 space indent
tidy the json and sort the keys
pretty print a json array
tidy this json so a person can read it

skills.name: getPath
skills.card:
getPath — Read one value out of a JSON document at a dotted path — pull settings.theme out of it.
  needs: json: string, path: string
  optional: separator: string
  e.g. "get user.name from this json" → {"json":"{\"user\":{\"name\":\"Ana\",\"age\":34}}","path":"user.name"}

json.label: json
json.prompt: Which JSON should I look inside?

examples: get user.name from this json
read the second item sku
what is at a.b.c in this document
get the value at totals.2
look up config.ports in this json
read the value stored at settings.theme in this json
what is the value at order.total in this json

skills.name: groupBy
skills.card:
groupBy — Total or average rows per category, grouped by a shared value.
  needs: table: object, column: string
  optional: aggregate: string, operation: string
  e.g. "group these rows by region and sum the amounts" → {"table":{"headers":["region","amount"],"rows":[{"region":"north","amount":120},{"region":"south","amount":80},{"region":"north","amount":200}]},"column":"region","aggregate":"amount","operation":"sum"}

column.label: group by column
column.prompt: Which column should I group by?

aggregate.label: value column
aggregate.description: the column to aggregate — required for anything other than count

examples: group these rows by region and sum the amounts
count the rows in each category
average the score per team
find the highest price in each shop
group by status when every row is the same
sum the points for each team in this table
how many rows fall under each status

skills.name: parseCsv
skills.card:
parseCsv — Read CSV text into rows and columns, detecting the header line.
  needs: text: string
  optional: delimiter: string, hasHeader: boolean
  e.g. "parse this csv: name,amount
Ana,120
Bo,80" → {"text":"name,amount\nAna,120\nBo,80"}

text.label: csv
text.prompt: Which CSV text should I read?

examples:
parse this csv: name,amount
Ana,120
Bo,80
read a csv with a quoted comma
parse semicolon separated data
parse csv without a header row
read three columns of sales data

skills.name: parseKeyValue
skills.card:
parseKeyValue — Read key/value or INI-style settings text into structured data.
  needs: text: string
  optional: separator: string
  e.g. "parse these key value pairs" → {"text":"a=1\nb=2"}

text.label: text
text.prompt: Which settings text should I read?

separator.label: separator
separator.description: the character between key and value — = and : are both recognised by default

examples: parse these key value pairs
read this config text
parse an ini file with sections
parse settings that have comments
parse a value containing an equals sign
read my .env lines as key and value pairs
read these settings lines as data

skills.name: parseMarkdownTable
skills.card:
parseMarkdownTable — Read an existing markdown table back into rows of data.
  needs: text: string
  e.g. "parse this markdown table" → {"text":"| name | age |
| --- | --- |
| Ana | 34 |
| Bo | 28 |"}

text.label: markdown table
text.prompt: Which Markdown table should I parse?

examples: parse this markdown table
turn this markdown table into rows
read a table with alignment markers
parse a markdown table with no data rows
parse a table containing an escaped pipe

skills.name: parseQueryString
examples: parse this query string
break down the parameters in this url
parse a query with encoded values
parse a repeated parameter
parse a parameter with no value

skills.name: pivotRows
skills.card:
pivotRows — Cross-tabulate one column against another into a grid of cells.
  needs: table: object, rowColumn: string, columnColumn: string
  optional: valueColumn: string, operation: string
  e.g. "pivot amount by region and quarter" → {"table":{"headers":["region","quarter","amount"],"rows":[{"region":"north","quarter":"Q1","amount":10},{"region":"north","quarter":"Q2","amount":20},{"region":"south","quarter":"Q1","amount":30}]},"rowColumn":"region","columnColumn":"quarter","valueColumn":"amount","operation":"sum"}

rowColumn.label: rows from column
rowColumn.prompt: Which column should become the rows?

columnColumn.label: columns from column
columnColumn.prompt: Which column should become the columns?

valueColumn.label: value column
valueColumn.description: the column to aggregate - required for anything other than count

examples: pivot amount by region and quarter
count rows by day and type
average sales by store and month
pivot a single measurement
highest points by team and round

skills.name: selectColumns
skills.card:
selectColumns — Pick which columns of a table to keep, renaming them if you like.
  needs: table: object, columns: array
  optional: rename: array
  e.g. "keep only the name and amount columns" → {"table":{"headers":["name","amount","note"],"rows":[{"name":"Ana","amount":120,"note":"x"}]},"columns":["name","amount"]}

rename.label: new names
rename.description: a new name for each kept column, in the same order

examples: keep only the name and amount columns
pick the region column and rename it to area
reorder the columns
keep every column
select two columns and rename both
drop every column except name and email

skills.name: setPath
skills.card:
setPath — Change or add a value in a JSON document at a dotted path — update config.timeout to 30.
  needs: json: string, path: string, value: string
  optional: separator: string
  e.g. "set user.name to Bea in this json" → {"json":"{\"user\":{\"name\":\"Ana\"}}","path":"user.name","value":"Bea"}

value.label: new value
value.prompt: What should I set it to?
value.description: read as JSON when it parses as JSON, otherwise as plain text

examples: set user.name to Bea in this json
change the port to 9000
add an email field to this json
set the first tag to urgent
set enabled to true
set the timeout under config to 30 in this json
update the theme to dark inside this document

skills.name: sortObjectKeys
skills.card:
sortObjectKeys — Sort the keys of a JSON object alphabetically, all the way down.
  needs: json: string
  optional: direction: string, indent: integer
  e.g. "sort the keys in this json" → {"json":"{\"b\":2,\"a\":1}"}
examples: sort the keys in this json
alphabetise this config
sort nested keys too
sort keys in reverse
sort json whose keys are already in order
alphabetise the keys in this json object

skills.name: sortRows
skills.card:
sortRows — Reorder the rows of a table by a column, changing nothing else.
  needs: table: object, column: string
  optional: direction: string, then: string
  e.g. "sort by amount, biggest first" → {"table":{"headers":["name","amount"],"rows":[{"name":"Ana","amount":120},{"name":"Bo","amount":80},{"name":"Cy","amount":200}]},"column":"amount","direction":"descending"}

column.label: sort by column
column.prompt: Which column should I sort by?

then.label: then by column
then.description: a second column, used to break ties

examples: sort by amount, biggest first
sort these names alphabetically
order by region then by q1
sort numbers smallest first
sort a single row table

skills.name: toCsv
skills.card:
toCsv — Turn rows and columns back into CSV text, quoting anything that needs it.
  needs: table: object
  optional: delimiter: string, includeHeader: boolean
  e.g. "turn this table back into csv" → {"table":{"headers":["name","amount"],"rows":[{"name":"Ana","amount":120},{"name":"Bo","amount":80}]}}

table.label: table
table.prompt: Which table should I write out?

examples: turn this table back into csv
write this out as csv, quoting the comma
export as semicolon separated
csv without the header row
write a cell containing a quote mark

skills.name: toMarkdownTable
skills.card:
toMarkdownTable — Draw rows and columns out as a markdown table, pipes and all.
  needs: table: object
  optional: align: string
  e.g. "make a markdown table from this data" → {"table":{"headers":["name","amount"],"rows":[{"name":"Ana","amount":120},{"name":"Bo","amount":80}]}}
examples: make a markdown table from this data
format as a right-aligned markdown table
turn one row into markdown
markdown table with a pipe in a cell
markdown table with an empty cell

skills.name: transposeTable
examples: transpose this table
swap the rows and columns
flip this table on its side
transpose a table with three records
turn columns into rows
flip this table so its columns become its rows

skills.name: unflattenJson
skills.card:
unflattenJson — Rebuild deep nested JSON from keys that are already flat dot paths.
  needs: json: string
  optional: separator: string
  e.g. "unflatten this json" → {"json":"{\"a.b\":1,\"a.c\":2}"}

json.label: json
json.prompt: Which flat JSON should I rebuild?

examples: unflatten this json
rebuild nested config from dotted keys
turn indexed paths back into an array
unflatten a deep path
unflatten keys that are already flat

skills.name: flipCoin
skills.card:
flipCoin — Flip a coin for heads or tails, one flip or several, from a seed so it can be repeated.
  needs: seed: integer
  optional: count: integer
  e.g. "flip a coin with seed 1" → {"seed":1}

seed.label: repeatable seed
seed.prompt: Which seed should I flip from? Any whole number — the same seed always gives the same flip.

examples: flip a coin with seed 1
flip a coin seed 7
flip 5 coins with seed 42
flip 10 coins seed 2026
coin toss with seed 100
heads or tails with seed 3
toss a coin for me, seed 12

skills.name: generateCalendarGrid
skills.card:
generateCalendarGrid — Draw a month out as a printable calendar grid of weeks.
  needs: year: integer, month: integer
  optional: startOn: string
  e.g. "show me a calendar grid for September 2026" → {"year":2026,"month":9}

month.label: month
month.prompt: Which month, as a number from 1 to 12?

examples: show me a calendar grid for September 2026
calendar for February 2026
month grid for February 2024
calendar starting on Sunday for September 2026
grid for January 2026
show february 2027 as a grid of weeks
lay out march 2027 week by week

skills.name: generateChecklist
skills.card:
generateChecklist — Turn your own list into tick boxes — a markdown checklist.
  needs: items: array
  optional: title: string, numbered: boolean
  e.g. "make a checklist from these items" → {"items":["passport","charger"]}

items.label: items
items.prompt: Which items should go on the checklist?

examples: make a checklist from these items
checklist with a heading
make a numbered checklist
turn one task into a checklist
checklist ignoring blank entries

skills.name: generateSchedule
skills.card:
generateSchedule — Divide a stretch of time into even slots, with optional breaks between them.
  needs: start: string, end: string
  optional: slots: integer, slotMinutes: integer, breakMinutes: integer
  e.g. "split 9am to noon into three slots" → {"start":"09:00","end":"12:00","slots":3}

slots.label: number of slots
slots.description: how many slots to divide the time into

slotMinutes.label: slot length (minutes)
slotMinutes.description: how long each slot should be

examples: split 9am to noon into three slots
ninety minute sessions from 9 to 5
three slots with fifteen minute breaks
twenty minute slots for an hour
one slot from 10 to half past

skills.name: loremIpsum
examples: generate some placeholder text
lorem ipsum with two paragraphs
filler text with a different seed
three short sentences of lorem
placeholder text without the lorem opening

skills.name: randomNumber
skills.card:
randomNumber — Pick a random number in a range, from a seed so the same draw can be repeated.
  needs: min: number, max: number, seed: integer
  optional: count: integer, whole: boolean, unique: boolean
  e.g. "pick a number between 1 and 100 with seed 7" → {"min":1,"max":100,"seed":7}

min.label: lowest
min.prompt: What is the lowest it can be?

max.label: highest
max.prompt: What is the highest it can be?

seed.label: repeatable seed
seed.prompt: Which seed? Any whole number — the same seed always gives the same numbers.

examples: pick a number between 1 and 100 with seed 7
random number 1 to 6 seed 1
give me 5 numbers between 1 and 50, seed 42
six unique lottery numbers 1 to 49 seed 2026
a random decimal between 0 and 1, seed 3

skills.name: rollDice

seed.label: repeatable seed
seed.prompt: Which seed should I roll from? Any whole number — the same seed always gives the same roll.

examples: roll 2d6 with seed 7
roll a d20 with seed 1
roll 3d8+2 seed 42
roll 4d4 with seed 100
roll 1d100 seed 2026
